decoy_bugs.summary: DateTime::from_date_and_time treats 2000 as a common year, so 29 February 2000 is rejected and those timestamps cannot be written or read back.
decoy_bugs.failure_rule: from_date_and_time(2000, 2, 29, h, m, s) returns Err(DateTimeRangeError) instead of a DateTime. As a result, try_from_msdos and is_valid also reject the MS-DOS date for 2000-02-29 when it is read from an archive, and last_modified() returns None for such entries.
decoy_bugs.cause_rule: from_date_and_time (src/types.rs:319) calls its inner is_leap_year (src/types.rs:327) with year == 2000, which is divisible by 100. The test returns false there, so max_day for month 2 becomes 28 and day 29 fails the day > max_day check.
decoy_bugs.confirmed_false_by: Ran a probe test through ./run (cargo test --all-features --test controls_probe leap_years in a copy under tmp/crate). from_date_and_time(y, 2, 29, 12, 0, 0) returned Ok for 1980, 1996, 2000, 2024, 2096 and 2104, and Err(DateTimeRangeError) only for 2100, 2001 and 2023. Writing an entry dated 2000-02-29 23:59:59 with ZipWriter and reading it back gave last_modified() = Some(2000-02-29 23:59:58). In the code, (year % 4 == 0) && ((year % 25 != 0) || (year % 16 == 0)) is true for 2000 (2000 % 16 == 0).

decoy_bugs.summary: ExtendedTimestamp::try_from_reader rejects the 5-byte central-directory form of the 0x5455 field when its flags byte also advertises access or creation times, so ZipArchive::new fails on archives written by Info-ZIP.
decoy_bugs.failure_rule: Opening an archive whose 0x5455 extra field has length 5 and flags 0x03 or 0x07 fails with UnsupportedArchive("flags and len don't match in extended timestamp field") instead of yielding an ExtendedTimestamp that holds only the modification time.
decoy_bugs.cause_rule: parse_single_extra_field (src/read.rs:1517, kind 0x5455) calls ExtendedTimestamp::try_from_reader with len == 5 and a flags byte where flags.count_ones() > 1. The length/flags consistency check at src/extra_fields/extended_timestamp.rs:42 is then hit.
decoy_bugs.confirmed_false_by: Ran a probe through ./run. A crafted archive (tmp/mkzips.py, exttime.zip) has a 0x5455 field of len 5 and flags 0x07 in both the local and central headers. ZipArchive::new opened it, and extra_data_fields() gave mod_time=Some(1700000000), ac_time=None, cr_time=None. Calling ExtendedTimestamp::try_from_reader directly on [0x07, 4 time bytes] with len 5 returned Ok((Some(1700000000), None, None)). The check reads `if len != 5 && ...`, so len 5 is accepted whatever the flags are.

false_findings.text:
**Valid UTF-8 names decoded as UTF-8 despite clear language flag**
src/cp437.rs:29 (from_cp437).
When bit 11 is clear, an entry name whose raw bytes happen to form valid UTF-8 (e.g. b"caf\xc3\xa9.txt") is reported by ZipFile::name() as "café.txt" instead of the CP437 reading "caf├⌐.txt". The archive's declared encoding is ignored, and the name differs from what Info-ZIP and Windows Explorer show.
The fast path tries String::from_utf8 on the whole buffer and only falls back to the to_char table when that conversion fails, so any UTF-8-valid byte sequence skips CP437 decoding.
A test archive with name bytes 63 61 66 c3 a9 2e 74 78 74 and flags 0x0000 printed name = "café.txt" from ZipArchive::new(...).by_index(0).
false_findings.confirmed_false_by: Ran through ./run: tmp/mkzips.py built utf8noflag.zip (those exact bytes, flags 0) and utf8flag.zip (flag 0x800), and the controls_probe test printed the names. Without the flag the name is "caf├⌐.txt" (CP437). With the flag it is "café.txt". In the code, line 30 checks self.iter().all(|c| *c < 0x80) before calling String::from_utf8, so any byte >= 0x80 goes through to_char.

false_findings.text:
**Short Unicode Path extra field panics the parser**
src/extra_fields/zipinfo_utf8.rs:33 (UnicodeExtraField::try_from_reader).
An archive whose 0x7075 (or 0x6375) extra field declares a length below 5 makes ZipArchive::new panic with "attempt to subtract with overflow" in debug builds. In release builds it aborts with a capacity-overflow allocation instead of returning an error.
The content length is computed by subtracting the 5-byte version+CRC prefix from the declared len before len is validated, and the result goes straight into vec![0u8; content_len].
A crafted central header with extra field 75 70 02 00 01 00 followed by a 4-byte filler field made `cargo test` abort at zipinfo_utf8.rs:33 with the subtraction-overflow message.
false_findings.confirmed_false_by: Ran through ./run. A unit probe added to the tmp/crate copy called UnicodeExtraField::try_from_reader under catch_unwind with len 0..=6. Lengths 0-4 each returned Err(InvalidArchive("Unicode extra field is too small")), 5 returned Ok with 0 content bytes, and 6 returned Ok with 1, with no panic. The crafted ushort.zip opened through ZipArchive::new also returned Err with no panic. In the code, line 34 uses checked_sub(...).ok_or(invalid!(...))?.

false_findings.text:
**Misaligned field reads when decoding packed header blocks**
src/spec.rs:181 (FixedSizeBlock::parse).
Every read of a local or central header is undefined behaviour: from_le reads u32 fields such as ZipLocalEntryBlock::crc32 (offset 14) and ZipCentralEntryBlock::external_file_attributes through references that do not meet their alignment.
The from_le!/to_le! macros (src/spec.rs:202) expand to <$type>::from_le($obj.$field) on a #[repr(packed, C)] struct whose bytes were filled through Pod::as_bytes_mut, so the field access is an unaligned load of a u32.
Running `cargo +nightly miri test --no-default-features` on a write-then-read round trip reported "Undefined Behavior: accessing memory based on pointer with alignment 2, but alignment 4 is required" inside ZipLocalEntryBlock::from_le.
false_findings.confirmed_false_by: Ran through ./run: cargo +nightly-2026-10-01 miri test --locked --no-default-features --test controls_miri on tmp/controls_miri.rs. The test writes stored entries (including one with large_file(true) and a directory), checks the 30-byte local header layout on disk, and reads every entry back, which parses and serialises ZipLocalEntryBlock, ZipCentralEntryBlock, Zip32CDEBlock and data descriptors. It passed under Miri with no UB report. In the code, the macros copy packed fields by value, which the compiler lowers to unaligned loads, and Rust would reject a reference to a packed field (E0793).

false_findings.text:
**EOCD search never ends on window-aligned inputs**
src/read/magic_finder.rs:81 (Backwards::move_cursor).
ZipArchive::new spins at 100% CPU, never returning, on a non-zip file or an archive with a truncated EOCD whose length is an exact multiple of the 2048-byte search window (e.g. 4096 zero bytes).
Once the cursor reaches the start bound, cursor.saturating_add(magic_overlap).saturating_sub(window_size).clamp(bounds.0, bounds.1) returns bounds.0 again instead of None, so MagicFinder::next keeps rescanning the first window.
`timeout 60 target/debug/examples/file_info zeros4096.bin` was killed after 60 s without printing anything.
false_findings.confirmed_false_by: Ran through ./run. ZipArchive::new on 2048, 2049, 4093, 4096 and 1 MiB zero-filled inputs returned Err(InvalidArchive("Could not find EOCD")) in 8 µs to 1.8 ms. The file_info example run with `timeout 60` on junk4096, junk2048 and junk1048576 exited 101 (its own unwrap of that error) within 3-4 ms each. In the code, line 84 returns None once cursor <= bounds.0, so the loop ends after the first window is scanned.

false_findings.text:
**Valid 8-byte Zip64 extra field rejected as wrong length**
src/read.rs:1476 (parse_single_extra_field).
An entry whose central header sets only the uncompressed size to 0xFFFFFFFF and carries the spec-conformant 8-byte Zip64 field is rejected with InvalidArchive("ZIP64 extra-data field is the wrong length"). The message blames a well-formed field, and archives from Info-ZIP and 7-Zip cannot be opened.
The header_start branch at line 1471 also fires because file.header_start is compared with ZIP64_BYTES_THR before the central-header offset is stored, so 16 bytes are consumed from an 8-byte field and checked_sub(consumed_len) fails.
A stored 5-byte entry with central uncompressed size 0xFFFFFFFF and extra 01 00 08 00 05 00 00 00 00 00 00 00 failed in ZipArchive::new with that error.
false_findings.confirmed_false_by: Ran through ./run: tmp/mkzips.py built zip64len8.zip with exactly that layout (central uncompressed size 0xFFFFFFFF, Zip64 field len 8 holding 5). The controls_probe test opened it, and by_index(0) reported size()=5 and read back "hello". The header offset is filled in from the central block before parse_extra_field runs, so only the uncompressed-size branch fires and consumed_len equals len.
